name: Visual modality claim without matching interaction and keyboard exit
summary: A surface is represented as modal (especially aria-modal=true) while the background remains interactable or the focused user lacks a task-valid keyboard exit.
recurring_structure: A styled backdrop or floating container is treated as modal solely by visual treatment or role/aria-modal marking, without verifying background interaction isolation and a keyboard-only exit or choice path.
harm_mechanism: Users may be told by assistive-technology modality cues that outside content is unavailable when it is functionally reachable, or become unable to leave a focus-containing task by keyboard; conversely a visual backdrop cannot create native document-blocking inertness.
context: UI that intentionally claims an active modal dialog while controlling surrounding page interaction and user escape/choice.
applicability: Any aria-modal marked dialog where outside interactions are still available or there is no viable keyboard-only departure/choice path.
Any visually modal overlay whose expected native modal/inert guarantees are inferred only from CSS, role or callback wiring.
legitimate_contexts: A legitimately nonmodal popover or disclosure does not need modal background inertness and should not be judged against modal-specific focus-trap mechanics.
A correctly realized native HTML showModal() dialog may obtain native inertness via the documented algorithm, though browser/app behavior remains untested here.
A required-acknowledgment gate may suppress conventional Escape when an explicit accessible choice path is present; no blanket prohibition of force action follows.

usability: A user might act on background controls despite a visually exclusive task or encounter an interaction dead end; this is a mechanism hypothesis, not measured user harm.
accessibility: WCAG 2.1.2's conditional keyboard-only exit criterion may be implicated when no keyboard way out exists; APG warns incorrect aria-modal can hide outside content for some assistive technology users. No target-page failure was tested.
The HTML inertness algorithm is native showModal-specific; ARIA alone is not a platform interaction lock.
performance: No validated runtime/performance penalty. Consequences unknown.
maintainability: An architecture that conflates native showModal, APG aria-modal, CSS backdrop and pinned library callbacks can conceal missing state/exit handling during maintenance; no maintainability trial.

counterexamples.summary: An intentionally nonmodal HTML popover may expose background interaction and use manual dismissal; that is not a broken modal unless it falsely claims modality.
counterexamples.context: Native popover=manual or other correctly designated nonmodal surface.

counterexamples.summary: A forced-action acknowledgment may vary Escape/close controls if the user has an explicit task-valid choice and accessible keyboard path.
counterexamples.context: USWDS described forced-action acknowledgment, subject to real task-specific WCAG evaluation.

version_context: WCAG 2.2 2024-12-12 norm conditions O02; WAI APG modality guidance unpinned O13/O14; WHATWG native algorithms living O07/O08/O12; pinned Primer code O31/O32/O34 source only.
